messages:
acme_james: Hey team — customers on Acme are seeing streaming outputs cut off midway. They use our hosted streaming endpoint via an API gateway that terminates HTTP/2 and talks to our backend over HTTP/1.1. Behavior: first ~200 tokens stream fine, then client receives a FIN and nothing else. No error payload. They say re-establishing the connection often returns the remainder of the response as a new stream chunk, but sometimes it's missing.

lina_support: Thanks @acme_james — can you paste the request snippet and whether they're using SSE or chunked encoding? Also include any proxy (ALB/NGINX/Envoy) between them and Redwood.

acme_james: They call streaming with SSE: GET /v1/streams?model=redwood-x & Authorization header. Using ALB in front -> ALB terminates TLS and forwards to our NLB which hits your public endpoint. Client is browser using EventSource. No explicit reconnect logic besides EventSource.

elaine_eng-runtime: Noted. Two likely culprits: 1) HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1 conversion causing intermediate buffering/FIN; 2) proxy connection idle/timeouts or proxy transforming transfer encoding. EventSource relies on chunked or text/event-stream staying open. If the gateway converts to request with Content-Length or buffers response until end, client will see odd behavior.

raj_infra: Can we get a server-side trace for that session? @support-bot can you pull request logs for ts 2026-04-10T14:12:03Z from ingress and runtime?

support-bot: Pulled logs for trace id 6a2f... Found upstream TCP FIN at 14:12:07Z. Backend runtime continued producing tokens until 14:12:09Z. There is a 2s gap between last token logged by runtime and TCP close from gateway.

devops_nginx: ALB->NLB shouldn't do HTTP/2->1 conversion on responses, but some customers put a gRPC gateway or API management layer that speaks h2 to clients and h1 upstream. Those can active-close streams when idle or on multiplex limits. Any sign of GOAWAYs?

elaine_eng-runtime: Good point. Also check if the gateway is doing response buffering (e.g., nginx proxy_buffering on) or setting proxy_http_version 1.1 but not using chunked transfer. If backend uses chunked but gateway eagerly sets Content-Length: 0 or switches to a transform that causes the browser to treat stream as ended.

acme_james: I asked customer to share raw network timeline; they attached HAR showing status 200 then event stream stopped after 2s. No final event.

lina_support: Repro plan — we need to replicate with an h2 client -> gateway -> h1 server. Steps: 1) Run a tiny server that streams SSE every 200ms for 5s (20 events). 2) Put Envoy or NGINX as a gateway configured for HTTP/2 frontend and HTTP/1.1 upstream. 3) Browser EventSource to gateway. Observe whether stream closes early.

elaine_eng-runtime: I'll drop a quick repro server you can run locally:
```bash
# simple node SSE server
node -e "const http=require('http');const server=http.createServer((req,res)=>{res.writeHead(200,{'Content-Type':'text/event-stream','Cache-Control':'no-cache','Connection':'keep-alive'});let i=0;const id=setInterval(()=>{i++;res.write(`data: token ${i}\n\n`);if(i>=20){clearInterval(id);res.end()}},200);});server.listen(9000);console.log('sse server on 9000');"
```
Then configure nginx with: `proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_buffering off; chunked_transfer_encoding on;` and `proxy_set_header Connection '';` Frontend: http2 on. Watch.

devops_nginx: Also try with Envoy: if http2 is used on frontend, ensure the cluster uses `use_http2 = false` and `common_http_protocol_options` aren't triggering stream half-closures. Envoy has aggressive stream idle timeouts by default on some configs.

acme_james: We tested with a local nginx and reproduced: stream stopped after ~200 tokens when nginx had `proxy_buffering on`. Turning it off made the browser receive the whole stream reliably.

raj_infra: Good reproduce. Two mitigation paths: 1) Advise customers to disable buffering on their gateway for SSE endpoints; 2) Provide a compatibility note: when using HTTP/2 front to clients and HTTP/1 upstream, ensure chunked encoding is preserved and proxy doesn't set content-length or close connection early.

elaine_eng-runtime: Additionally: implement idempotent reconnect tokens. If client's EventSource reconnects, we should support Range-like semantics for streaming tokens or have the server emit an ordered cursor so client can request missing tokens. For now add guidance: small keepalive comments (":\n") every 15s to keep intermediaries from considering stream idle. But careful: EventSource will see comments but they count as data and may still be buffered by some proxies unless proxy_buffering is off.

lina_support: Action items: 1) Lina: send customer a short KB explaining what to check on their gateway (disable buffering, chunked transfer, timeouts). 2) Elaine: open an eng-runtime ticket to add a short-lived reconnect cursor in the streaming protocol and add a keepalive ping. 3) Raj: add a note in our troubleshooting docs about common ALB/Envoy/Nginx pitfalls.

elaine_eng-runtime: For debugging, here's a curl invocation to emulate HTTP/2 client behavior:
```bash
# HTTP/2 client to gateway
curl -v --http2 https://gateway.example.com/v1/streams -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | sed -n '1,200p'
# Compare with HTTP/1.1 client
curl -v --http1.1 https://gateway.example.com/v1/streams -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | sed -n '1,200p'
```
Check for differences in headers: Transfer-Encoding, Content-Length, Connection, and any "x-envoy-decorator" or "x-nginx-proxy" headers.

devops_nginx: Also watch for intermediate devices doing connection pooling and closing idle upstream connections with active downstream streams — that causes backend to finish producing but client gets FIN. Observed in some managed API gateways.

acme_james: Customer confirmed they have an API mgmt layer that does transformations; they're rolling back that route to a raw ALB -> NLB path for a day to see if it fixes.

lina_support: Great. If they still see truncation after removing the mgmt layer, ping us and we'll gather packet captures and runtime traces. If fixed, we'll close the ticket with KB steps.

elaine_eng-runtime: I'll scope the runtime ticket: short-term add keepalive comments and make token stream resume-able by providing a monotonic token index in each event (e.g., `event: token\ndata: {"index":123,"text":"..."}\n\n`). Long-term: consider a small reconnect API to request from index N.

raj_infra: I've started a doc draft in #docs/troubleshooting that lists the config snippets for nginx/envoy/ALB to preserve streaming semantics. I'll push shortly.

acme_james: Thanks everyone — I'll update once customer finishes the rollback test.

lina_support: :thumbsup: Thanks team. Keeping thread open until customer confirms.
